title: Opinions & conversation repair
subtitle: Disagree and keep the exchange going
objectives: State an opinion with a reason and example.
Acknowledge a different position without falsely agreeing.
Use repair strategies during spontaneous discussion.
warmup: Retrieve two sentences and one repair strategy from c3-u10. Change the subject or situation in each sentence and explain what changed. Then read today’s objectives and predict where your existing language may be insufficient.

lectures.title: Separate position, support and scope
lectures.body: A useful opinion has a claim, a reason and an example: Creo que ampliar el horario ayudaría, porque algunas personas trabajan hasta tarde; por ejemplo…. Scope matters: a few comments do not establish what everyone wants. Use en mi experiencia or según la encuesta when that is the actual basis. Estoy de acuerdo en que… can identify common ground without agreeing with every conclusion. No estoy convencido de que… normally introduces a non-asserted conclusion with subjunctive. The aim is to make the relationship between evidence and opinion visible.

lectures.title: Repair is a collaborative skill
lectures.body: When comprehension fails, ask a focused question: ¿Te refieres al horario del sábado o al de toda la semana? A general ¿Qué? is sometimes enough, but a focused repair shows what you did understand. To reformulate your own point, use lo que quiero decir es…; to check, use si te entiendo bien…. Acknowledge correction explicitly and change course. Polite disagreement can remain direct: Entiendo la ventaja, pero me preocupa el costo. Do not fill every pause with memorized connectors; a short pause to think may produce a more relevant response than a fluent but unrelated sentence.

reading:
—Creo que deberíamos abrir los domingos porque algunas familias no pueden venir entre semana.
—Entiendo la ventaja, pero me preocupa el costo. No estoy convencida de que tengamos personal suficiente.
—¿Te refieres a todos los domingos o a una prueba de un mes?
—A un horario permanente. Una prueba limitada podría ser viable.
—Entonces coincidimos en explorar una prueba. Lo que quiero decir es que necesitamos escuchar a las familias antes de fijar el horario.
—De acuerdo. También habría que preguntar a quienes trabajan aquí.
Explica cómo una pregunta de aclaración cambia el desacuerdo y qué información falta antes de decidir.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: I think it would be useful.
quiz.explanation: “Creo que sería útil” expresses “I think it would be useful”. “No necesariamente” instead means “Not necessarily”. “Gracias por la corrección” instead means “Thank you for the correction”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: I am not convinced it is feasible.
options: No estoy convencida de que sea viable
answers: No estoy convencida de que sea viable
quiz.explanation: “No estoy convencida de que sea viable” expresses “I am not convinced it is feasible”. “Tenemos un punto en común” instead means “We have a point in common”. “¿En qué te basas?” instead means “What is your basis for that?”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: What I mean is….
quiz.explanation: “Lo que quiero decir es…” expresses “What I mean is…”. “Podemos comprobarlo” instead means “We can check it”. “Nos falta información” instead means “We are missing information”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: If I understand you correctly.
quiz.explanation: “Si te entiendo bien” expresses “If I understand you correctly”. “Necesito aclarar mi idea” instead means “I need to clarify my idea”. “Creo que sería útil” instead means “I think it would be useful”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: I understand the advantage, but….
options: No estoy convencida de que sea viable
quiz.explanation: “Entiendo la ventaja, pero…” expresses “I understand the advantage, but…”. “No estoy convencida de que sea viable” instead means “I am not convinced it is feasible”. “Gracias por la corrección” instead means “Thank you for the correction”.

quiz.prompt: Match each English meaning to its Spanish expression. Use each expression once.
answers: ["Entiendo la ventaja, pero…","¿Te refieres al sábado?","No necesariamente"]
quiz.explanation: “Entiendo la ventaja, pero…” means “I understand the advantage, but…”. “¿Te refieres al sábado?” means “Do you mean Saturday?”. “No necesariamente” means “Not necessarily”. Each alternative belongs to a different meaning; check the whole phrase, including its grammatical person and register.

This is the source model, not a text to submit unchanged. A successful adaptation retains the communicative purpose while changing relevant forms and facts. Compare with the worked examples for the reasons behind form choices.
homework.rubric: 0–3 each: fulfills the specified purpose; organized and comprehensible; target forms support meaning; revisions are explained with examples. 0 = no evidence, 1 = substantial help needed, 2 = effective with some support, 3 = independently effective for this task. Record who evaluated the work.

homework.prompt: Complete the resource assignment, or ask a willing reader to read the original text without showing it to you. First listen for the situation and purpose; listen again for three details and one contrast. Write a 60–100-word listening log naming the source, words actually heard, one uncertainty, and how you checked it. If using local synthesized speech, label it synthetic. Text-only preparation is not completed listening.
homework.model: A useful log separates the speaker’s message from your interpretation: “I heard [specific phrase]; I understood [claim]; I was uncertain about [word/relationship]; checking [text or partner] changed my interpretation to [correction].” Use the unit reading as an answer reference for a read-aloud version, never as evidence of an external speaker’s words.
homework.rubric: 0–2 each: identifies source and listening conditions; retrieves central meaning; supports three details; checks a specific uncertainty. Do not count a copied transcript as independent comprehension.

homework.prompt: Discuss whether a shared service should extend its hours. State a claim, give a reason, ask two focused follow-ups, and summarize the remaining disagreement fairly.
homework.model: Use the original reading/dialogue and the sentence-pattern cards as preparation. Make a brief outline, then put it away. Your partner should introduce a detail you did not prepare. Respond, request clarification if needed, and summarize what you agreed or still disagree about. Solo fallback: record two possible viewpoints and improvise a response after a pause; label it rehearsal.
homework.rubric: 0–3 each: task fulfillment, comprehensibility, control of target language, responsiveness to another speaker. A partner or instructor should cite one example per score. Solo rehearsal provides no evidence for live responsiveness; mark that dimension not observed.

homework.prompt: On a later day, retrieve six cards without looking. Use three in a fresh response to the practical task. Identify one recurring form error and one communication difficulty. Produce a corrected example, explain the reason, and schedule a specific follow-up exchange or listening session.
homework.model: Compare your response with these two models: Creo que sería útil / No estoy convencida de que sea viable. A useful reflection explains the function, not just the spelling. Revisit the first worked item and create a different example of its principle.
homework.rubric: Report recall count separately from performance. Reflection is complete when it contains an observed difficulty, an explained correction, a fresh example, and an actionable next session.

task: Discuss whether a shared service should extend its hours. State a claim, give a reason, ask two focused follow-ups, and summarize the remaining disagreement fairly.
culture: Turn-taking and overlap vary by setting. Do not interpret every overlap as hostility or every silence as agreement. Ask how the group wants to structure discussion, especially when people have different communication styles.
selfAssessment: I can state an opinion with a reason and example.
I can acknowledge a different position without falsely agreeing.
I can use repair strategies during spontaneous discussion.
remediation: Sort mistakes by form, meaning, and interaction. For form errors, explain a worked example and create a contrasting pair. For comprehension errors, replay a short segment or use a willing reader and verify your interpretation. For interaction difficulties, repeat the practical task with one new constraint. Compare evidence across days; repeated selection of a known answer alone is not mastery.
